key_insight: Expandable modality-specific experts enable medical vision-language learning across imaging domains while preserving existing representations when their computation paths remain unchanged.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support reusable image classification and retrieval tools across medical specialties, but clinical utility is not established by these benchmarks.
method: Combine shared visual computation, deterministically routed modality experts, and a separate text pathway.
Pretrain on unpaired images with modality-aware tokenization, then align image and text representations using paired data.
Add fundus and OCT experts while freezing the original image and text embedding paths.
evidence_signal: Training used 19.4 million unpaired image rows and 3.23 million image-text pairs; evaluation across nine modalities achieved best or tied-best results in 24 of 25 settings.
watch_item: Retention depends on unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions; feature-identity checks verify preservation only on evaluated inputs.
paper_title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
